[College group, 9:14 pm]
Sameer: [reel: rooftop infinity pool, Dubai skyline] good times 🥂
Tushar: bhai owns half of Gurgaon now, look at this lifestyle
Sameer: expanding soon boys, watch this space 😎
---
[DM, 11:52 pm]
Sameer: Faisal, quick thing. asking for a friend — any openings in your company? operations or general management side. 15-18 LPA bracket is fine.
Sameer: he's looking to move this month itself. solid guy, ran his own setup for years.
Sameer: and yaar don't bring this up in the group, he's private about it.
Faisal: arre sure sure, I'll check with HR on Monday 👍
---
[College group, next day, 1:30 pm]
Faisal: reunion venue sorted then — Sameer bhai will sponsor, business is booming 😂
Tushar: 😂😂 gym king
Sameer: 👍
---
[DM, three days later]
Faisal: hey, HR asked for the friend's CV, can you send?
Faisal: hello? bhai?

---
1. Who is the "friend" in Sameer's DM and how do you know? What is the third-person framing doing for Sameer — why this exact costume?
2. Trace what Faisal's group message on the next day did to Sameer. Why did the DM go silent — connect the thumbs-up, the joke, and the three-day silence.
3. Write the DM Faisal should send now, exactly as he should send it, that gets Sameer real help without ever making him admit anything.

# 1. The "Friend" Is Sameer Himself

Every line in the DM points back at Sameer. He says the friend "ran his own setup for years" — which is exactly the image Sameer projects in the group ("expanding soon boys"). He wants to move "this month itself" — that kind of urgency belongs to someone whose own situation is deteriorating, not to a casual middleman. And his insistence that Faisal "don't bring this up in the group" isn't about protecting a friend's privacy — it's about protecting the Dubai-pool, half-of-Gurgaon persona he just posted hours earlier. The salary range itself is a tell: 15–18 LPA is a respectable mid-career salary, not the income of someone who "owns half of Gurgaon." The gap between the group image and the DM reality is the whole story.

**Why the third-person costume?** Because "asking for a friend" is a reversible claim. If Faisal comes through, great — Sameer gets a lifeline. If nothing works out, no one ever heard Sameer admit he needs a job. He never said "I'm struggling." He never broke character. The third person is a firewall between the persona and the person. It lets him reach for help without surrendering the identity he's built in front of the people whose respect he's dependent on. It's not deception for fun — it's survival wrapped in slang.

---

# 2. The Chain Reaction: Joke → Thumbs-Up → Silence

Faisal's group message the next afternoon — *"Sameer bhai will sponsor, business is booming 😂"* — landed on exactly the fault line Sameer was trying to hide. Faisal almost certainly didn't mean it cruelly; he was riffing on the image Sameer himself created. But for Sameer, in the middle of quietly asking for a 15 LPA job, being publicly crowned as the guy whose business is "booming" was not a compliment. It was a tightening of the mask. It made the persona heavier, not lighter.

**The 👍** in the group is the tell. Sameer is the guy who posts 🥂 and 😎 and "watch this space." A bare thumbs-up from him is not engagement — it's minimal compliance. It says *I saw it, I can't laugh at this, I can't push back either, so here's the smallest possible signal that I'm still here.*

**The three-day DM silence** follows from the same knot. When Faisal follows up asking for the friend's CV, Sameer goes quiet — because sending a CV would force the fiction to produce evidence. Whose CV is it? If it's his own, the third-person costume falls apart. If he fabricates one, he's in deeper. The group joke made the public image feel even more load-bearing, so the private negotiation became even harder to continue. The silence isn't indifference. It's paralysis — the gap between who he's pretending to be and what he actually needs just got wider, and he doesn't know how to cross it without someone watching.

---

# 3. The DM Faisal Should Send

> *bhai — just checking in on the friend thing whenever you're ready, no rush at all. HR said even a LinkedIn profile works, doesn't have to be a formal CV. I can just forward it quietly, no application portal, no process — just a direct handoff. Tell him we'll keep it completely between us. Whatever works for him 🤝*

**Why this exact message works:**

- **"No rush at all"** — removes the time
